key: Hear me, O LORD, hear me, that this people may know that Thou, LORD, art God, for Thou didst turn their heart backward.
s: On Carmel, before the fire falls and he slays Baal’s prophets at the Kishon, Elijah prays; Rashi, on 18:37, reads ‘turn their heart’ as God leaving them room to stray, though He could have set their hearts toward Him, and Metzudat David, on 18:37, as a past for a future: by the sign He will turn them back.

evidence.gloss: [Rashi on 18:37, on ‘and Thou didst turn their heart’:] You gave them room to turn away from following You, and it was in Your hand to set their heart toward You. … [Metzudat David on 18:37:] A past in place of a future, meaning: by this miracle You will turn their heart to You, which until now was backward, turned away from You.

reason: verse.js ok, ref 1 Kings 18:37 and at [304,37] match. Plain sense faithful: 18:30 to 36 Elijah rebuilds the altar on Carmel and prays; 18:38 the fire falls; 18:40 the prophets of Baal are slain at the brook Kishon; no four-word run from the key. Opened every packet source on 18:37. Rashi’s own Hebrew (not only the Metsudah English) says God gave them room to turn away though it was in His hand to set their heart toward Him; Metzudat David reads הסבות as a past standing for a future: by this miracle You will turn their heart back to You. The two genuinely differ (a past permission versus a future turning), named without resolving. ‘by the sign’ renders הנס acceptably. Source line names the Hebrew edition read for each commentator. entry-check ok on scratch/V-d114-p.json.
